column3: Viewed q_spt1_h2 + calib. Real GRT q_spt0 a10 FAIL with 962,945 overflow (dominant M3; 44% on the S face), the worst HBM type. They run under and between the two xcal macros and through the S pin field. pv1 also has L5076x2 (653 b) on y 8.6.

column11: Form E1, positions only: each chain goes face -> up to the macro-free row y 420 (above the 250-um macros) -> along -> down. Register counts and cycles are unchanged, hops <= 395 um. L1271 keeps S0 at the pin and its S0->S1 stays <= 405. pv1 L5076x2 has only 4 registers and already fails G0 in d49a (S0->S1 759 > 405); it is the remaining pv1 hot bin. Structural fix (AMENDMENT 4): +1 station on L5076 (latency row owned by DIE-HBM). With 5 registers on the y 140 row, hops are 343 um and the trial pv1 p99 = 0.961.

column11: 7.5 kbit of die transit crosses a 2065-um type with 2 macro rows. Positions-only forms stop at p99 1.19-1.28, now in the open V/M3 channel, and the rule is p99 > 1 = FAIL. Structural fix: carry L8100/L8101/L1237 in a die ft band beside su30 (die re-site, DIE-HBM-100 / DIE-LAYOUT-HBM), or add a +1-cycle relay row so the transit splits into 2 narrower channels. I will not build a p99 > 1 form.

column3: Viewed q_b100pv1_d14: logic in the top band, taps on macros. route_supply q_b100 9.50 (street_V M3); b102 has face V 7.7 on the E/W ring-bus pins. Each type holds 8 units: h1 218.6x187.5 + ra/rb 106.3x290.3 each. Macro area 821k um2 in 708-734 x 1555 (frac 0.72-0.78). The broadcast hid2/key nets go to all 24 cores.
column11: DIE-LAYOUT-HBM asked (W' not composable) for a continuous V street >= 150 um inside the fixed outlines. Arithmetic: the macros need >= 528 um of column width over 1555 um. 528 + 150 = 678 against 708, so the rest would have to pack at about 95%, and the unit heights (187.5 / 290.3) bin-pack to >= 644 + 150 = 794 > 708. Infeasible without squeezing. Options under study: unit-local stacking (each h1 abutted on its own ra|rb pair, 3 unit columns 3/3/2) with the broadcast spine in a street; or move 1-2 units per type (outline/arch).
